title: Environment variables, per-environment configuration and secrets

videos.script: agenda's code carries facts about one machine. Debug on. A secret key anybody with the code can read. A database reached as you. {{title}} On a server, each of those is wrong, and two are dangerous. {{wrong}} So the values that change between machines move into the environment, and the code reads them from there. {{environ}} A missing secret key stops the application at start-up. A missing debug flag means off. Each default is chosen to fail on the safe side. {{defaults}} Each application gets a database role of its own, with a generated password, over TCP. You meet peer authentication refusing it on the socket. {{role}} FastAPI reads its settings through pydantic-settings, and a secret prints as stars. Rotate the token key, and every old token stops working. {{settings}} The file with the secrets never enters git. And Django's deployment check names what is still missing: debug, allowed hosts, and four things about HTTPS.
